identity.title: Long-Form Speech Generation with Spoken Language Models

problem.claim: Generate coherent speech lasting multiple minutes for multimedia generation and audio-native voice assistants.

gap.claim: Existing textless spoken language models struggle beyond tens of seconds because of speech-token temporal resolution, long-sequence modeling or extrapolation issues, and inference memory costs.

contributions.claim: SpeechSSM, a family of spoken language models for learning from and sampling long-form spoken audio without text intermediates.
LibriSpeech-Long, embedding-based and LLM-judged metrics, and quality measurements over generation length and time for long-form speech evaluation.
The authors provide speech samples and the LibriSpeech-Long dataset, with code or model releases described as future possibilities.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe SpeechSSM as the first speech language model family to learn from and sample long-form spoken audio in a single decoding session without text intermediates.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that SpeechSSM can sample examples such as 16 minutes of read or extemporaneous speech in one decoding session without text intermediates.
The authors report that SpeechSSMs greatly surpass current Transformer spoken language models in coherence and efficiency on multi-minute generations while matching them at the utterance level.
The authors report that existing spoken-language evaluations were uninformative for the new long-form setting, motivating their benchmark and metric additions.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper targets generative speech modeling over multiple minutes for long-form multimedia and audio-native assistants.
It identifies coherence, long-sequence architecture, extrapolation, and inference-memory obstacles that limit existing textless spoken models beyond tens of seconds.
It introduces SpeechSSM for long-form spoken-audio learning and single-session sampling without text intermediates.
It reports comparisons with Transformer spoken LMs, adds long-form evaluation resources, and points to released samples and dataset access.

source_observation.claim: The authors state that current evaluations were uninformative in the long-form setting and therefore introduce a dedicated benchmark, multiple metric types, and measurements across length and time.

lessons.interpretation: Evaluation design may need to change when the target capability introduces a new failure dimension, such as degradation over duration.
lessons.application: When proposing a long-horizon generator, pair standard local-quality metrics with a task-specific benchmark and explicitly track quality as sequence length increases.
lessons.exception: This move may be unnecessary when the application has no meaningful horizon-dependent behavior or when validated task-specific evaluations already exist.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative scores, sample-selection details, or precise definitions for coherence, efficiency, or utterance-level matching.
It does not specify the SpeechSSM architecture, training setup, dataset scale, metric implementation, or comparison conditions.
Code and model releases are described as future possibilities, so their availability is not established by the abstract.
